section.title: 新闻 3
section.preview: Denver is suspending its popular electric bike incentive program.

lines.text: Denver is suspending its popular electric bike incentive program.
The program was launched in April.
It allowed Denver residents to apply for $400 in government funds before buying an electric bike from a participating shop.
Residents who met certain income qualifications could qualify for $1,200.
More than 3,000 Denver residents applied for incentives within the first three weeks.
The city then changed the program to limit the number of applications each month.
On Monday, the city announced the pause.
We're honored to be a part of transforming the way Denver wants to move around, said Grace Rink, Denver's Chief Climate Officer.
We exhausted three years' worth of funding in six months.
The city said the program has put 4,400 electric bikes on the streets of Denver and invested $8.6 million into the local economy.
The city has provided 2,200 incentives to lower-income residents.
That represents 68% of the program funding.
The City expects to resume the program early next year.
It also plans design changes to make participation easier and increase access to the program.
